title: Short-session throughput sag after routing heuristics change — hotpatch and customer escalations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
After the 2026-03-10 deployment of adaptive-batching-v2 + stride-kernel-selector, we started observing a regression affecting short interactive sessions (prompt length < 32 tokens): first token time (TTFT) increased by ~2.5x for affected requests and sustained tokens/sec dropped ~40% under mild load. Impact spans Hosted and Dedicated customers using multi-model routing; several enterprise customers in APAC reported production failures and opened escalations. Private/VPC customers saw similar behavior in environments that enabled the new batching heuristics.

Scope: Hosted API (region: us-west2, eu-west1), Dedicated clusters with multiplex routing, and Private installs that opted-in to adaptive-batching-v2. Regression appears workload-dependent (high proportion of short, low-token-rate sessions) and is more visible when model-fanout is >2.

Hypothesis: A combination of the stride-kernel change (changed kernel selection for small-seq paths) + the new microbatch handshake introduced extra scheduling jitter before first-token flush. This causes small requests to wait for batching windows that no longer align with observed session arrival patterns, increasing TTFT and reducing tokens/sec.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- 2026-03-12 09:30 UTC: rolled feature-flag to disable adaptive-batching-v2 for Hosted (flag: batching.short-session-disable).
- 2026-03-12 10:15 UTC: hotpatch runtime to force immediate microbatch flush for sessions with prompt_length < 48 on Dedicated pools (PR #2347).
- 2026-03-12 11:00 UTC: published interim guidance to Support/SEs and notified 3 affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for hotfix.

Current status:
- Metric recovery: partial; TTFT decreased to ~1.15x baseline for Hosted after flag toggle; Dedicated improved on patched clusters but Private customers running older runtime still affected.
- Root-cause engineering investigation ongoing. Patch in review to lift the handshake delay without reverting stride-kernel improvements (PR #2369).

Acceptance criteria for full resolution:
1) TTFT for small sessions returns to baseline +/-10% for both Hosted and Dedicated under 95th-percentile load patterns.
2) tokens/sec for affected workloads recovers to baseline +/-15%.
3) No regression introduced for long-context streaming sessions or heavy-batched throughput workloads.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge hotfix PR #2369 (force alignment of batching window with arrival distribution, sub-ms handshake path) after 2-approver review and CI green.
2) Canary to 5% Hosted traffic in us-west2 and one Dedicated cluster for 1 hour, monitor TTFT/tokens/sec/ops errors.
3) If canary stable, ramp to 50% over 30 minutes, then full roll in 2 hours.
4) For Private installs, publish signed patch bundle + upgrade instructions; offer assisted upgrade for enterprise customers.

Notes on trade-offs considered:
- Full rollback of stride-kernel-selector would restore baseline but loses throughput wins on long-context workloads. Team prioritized targeted short-session fixes to preserve overall throughput gains.
- Short-term forced flush increases CPU overhead slightly on edge workers; accepted for P0 customer impact until we can fine-tune heuristics.

Next steps:
- Complete PR review and run extended performance harness focusing on short-session mixes (Benchmark suite: perf-harness/short-session/2026-03).
- Contact Private customers with recommended config toggle; set up schedule for assisted deploys.
- Draft postmortem and instrumentation follow-ups (see action items).
